page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, operating at clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz. The CPU subsystem integrates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It is configured with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU memory-to-core ratio. The instance includes 161 GB of temporary local SSD storage and does not include a GPU.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-thread compute capabilities alongside multi-core constraints typical of a four-thread footprint. The instance achieved a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2,700.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,493.0. Multi-core performance is more limited, registering 3,363.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing and 21.84 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem demonstrated uncached large-block throughput of 37.42 GB/sec for reads and 22.82 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, the system completed 4.15 million Redis SET operations per second and handled static web serving at 5.05 GB/sec.

The E4ads_v5 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-centric deployments by offering substantial RAM capacity without requiring the provision of unnecessary compute cores. The integrated 161 GB local SSD provides high-speed scratch space directly on the host, avoiding auxiliary storage attachment overhead for temporary buffers. Primary hardware tradeoffs include moderate uncached memory bandwidth and restricted parallel processing power. This configuration is best suited for mid-sized relational databases, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, enterprise backend applications, and lightweight data staging pipelines.
